AfterObtained.rationale: BloodSoakedRose.cs:22-25 calls CardPileCmd.AddCurseToDeck<Enthralled>(owner), which delegates to AddCursesToDeck -- a loop that throws unless `curse.Type == CardType.Curse` and then performs an ordinary deck add. The type assertion is a developer guard, not behaviour, and Enthralled satisfies it on both sides (sts2_rl's enthralled is a CURSE). So the observable is a single Enthralled appended to the deck, which is what run.add_card(make_card('enthralled')) does. NOTE per binding rule 7: the AddCursesToDeck body is in CardPileCmd.cs, which this record does not hash.

ModifyMaxEnergy.rationale: EnergyVar(1).BaseValue added to the owner's max energy (BloodSoakedRose.cs:27-34) vs ENERGY = 1; BaseValue is the non-ascension read the contract pins, and no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension appears in the file. Same dispatcher and same turn position as relic/blessed_antler's and relic/bread's, and all three compose additively with no ordering sensitivity.

guards.rationale: The `player != base.Owner` / `shuffler == base.Owner` / `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player. The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState), so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

guards.what: N2: the Energy and Enthralled hover tips (BloodSoakedRose.cs:9-18)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

guards.what: N3: the +1 max Energy is unconditional -- it applies for the whole run, including the combat the Enthralled curse is drawn in
guards.rationale: Neither side gates the energy on anything (no turn check, no curse-in-hand check), so the relic is a flat +1 with a permanent deck cost. Recorded because relic/bread, audited in this same batch, has a nearly identical ModifyMaxEnergy that IS turn-gated, and the two are easy to conflate.
